title: Attribute Broker Integration and Evidence Guide
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document defines Redwood's standard for integrating an Attribute Broker (identity attribute translation/provisioning layer) with Redwood services, the minimal audit evidence required for compliance, data residency impacts, and the incident response procedures for broker-related compromises. It complements entitlement and audit playbooks by describing attribute mapping guarantees, evidence collection points, and secure test-and-rollout patterns for production.

Goals and scope:
- Provide a repeatable, auditable pattern for consuming attributes from external IdPs (SAML/OIDC) and provisioning systems (SCIM) into Redwood RBAC.
- Define evidence artifacts that satisfy internal and external audits (SOX/ISO/ SOC2 where applicable).
- Describe data residency and retention implications when attributes cross regions or include PII.
- Document incident handling and forensic steps specific to attribute broker failures or compromise.

Intended audience:
- Security engineers and compliance analysts
- Identity & Access Management (IAM) engineers
- Platform/product engineers integrating SSO/SCIM flows
- Audit/assurance owners

Core concepts and definitions:
- Attribute Broker: middleware service that normalizes identity assertions from IdPs (SAML/OIDC) and provisioning APIs (SCIM) into the canonical attribute model used by Redwood.
- Canonical attributes: a minimal set of attributes Redwood consumes for role mapping: user_id (opaque), email, org_id, department, role_claims (list), account_status, employee_type.
- Provisioning event: SCIM change or IdP assertion that results in creation, update, or deprovisioning of an account or entitlement mapping.
- Evidence artifact: stored record sufficient to demonstrate who requested or effected a change and what the system state was before/after.

Principles:
1) Immutable event capture: every provisioning event MUST generate an immutable audit record prior to downstream role changes. Records must include source, timestamp, actor, and a checksum of the incoming assertion.
2) Canonicalization at edge: attribute normalization is performed inside the broker; services consume only the canonical attribute payload to reduce downstream variance.
3) Minimal residency: PII in attributes is minimized and only the canonical ID and hashed email are stored where possible when crossing regions.
4) Evidence linkage: evidence artifacts MUST be linkable to the audit logging pipeline (trace_id) and stored with the same retention policy as access logs.

Required attributes and example mapping:
- Minimum canonical set (all required unless noted):
  - user_id: string (required)
  - email_hash: string (sha256, required)
  - org_id: string (required)
  - role_claims: list of strings (required)
  - account_status: enum [active,suspended,deleted] (required)
  - last_provisioned_at: iso8601 timestamp (required)
  - source_idp: string (optional)

Example SCIM incoming -> canonical broker output (JSON):
{
  "incoming_scim": {
    "userName": "j.smith@example.com",
    "externalId": "12345",
    "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User": {
      "department": "Platform"
    },
    "active": true
  },
  "canonical_output": {
    "user_id": "scim-12345",
    "email_hash": "sha256:d2c7...",
    "org_id": "acme-corp",
    "role_claims": ["developer","redwood-console"],
    "account_status": "active",
    "last_provisioned_at": "2025-03-02T14:22:01Z",
    "source_idp": "okta-acme"
  }
}

Audit evidence and storage requirements (table):
| Artifact | Contents | Retention | Storage location | Access controls |
|---------|----------|-----------|------------------|-----------------|
| Provisioning-event.json | raw assertion (masked PII), canonical output, trace_id, actor_id, ip | 7 years (enterprise) / 1 year (dev) | encrypted object store (s3://redwood-evidence/provisioning/) | role=auditor+security only, KMS key: projects/redwood/prod/evidence |
| Provisioning-checksum.meta | assertion checksum, broker-version, validation result | 7 years | same bucket | security/audit |
| Access-log entry | trace_id, service, action, result, latency | 3 years | centralized logging | logging-read roles, SIEM ingest |

Note: Dev/test PII minimization policy requires removing raw email in dev buckets; only email_hash is kept.

Integration checklist (pre-production):
1) Contract validation: verify IdP/SCIM schema against our canonical mapping.
2) Test harnessed assertions: run 1,000 synthetic provisioning events and verify canonicalization invariants (no missing user_id, role_claims not empty for employees).
3) Evidence pipeline: ensure provisioning-event.json and Provisioning-checksum.meta are emitted before role binding is applied.
4) Retention policy enforcement: validate lifecycle rules and KMS encryption key policies.
5) Cross-region gating: if org_id is flagged as cross-border, ensure email is hashed before replication.

Example SAML attribute mapping (XML snippet explained):
- Required attributes to request from IdP: Subject (NameID), eduPersonScopedAffiliation (or equivalent role), mail (if policy allows), org:unit.
- Broker will transform NameID -> user_id and mail -> email_hash.

Operational runbook: provisioning failures and rollbacks
1) Detection:
  - Alerting: Failures to canonicalize or failed checksum validation should create PagerDuty alert severity P2.
  - Monitoring signals: spike in "provisioning.errors" metric > 5% over 5m or repeated 401 responses from IdP.
2) Triage steps (Order matters):
  a) Identify trace_id(s) from the alert and open the provisioning-event artifact in the evidence store.
  b) Determine scope (single user, org, or global).
  c) If scope == org: place org in limited-access mode (see emergency ACL) and notify Customer Success for impacted customers.
  d) If scope == global: fail closed to prevent automated role grants and engage SRE and IAM.
3) Remediation:
  - Soft-fix: re-run canonicalization for impacted users from preserved raw assertions and reconcile role grants in the RBAC engine.
  - Hard rollback: if broker configuration change caused invalid mappings, revert broker config to previous tagged release and replay provisioning events from the last known-good checkpoint.
4) Evidence preservation: snapshot provisioning-event.json blobs for affected trace_ids and copy to immutable forensics bucket (retention 10 years for incidents).
5) Post-incident audit: produce a packet that includes timeline, artifact checksums, changed role bindings, rollbacks performed, and the mitigation plan. This packet becomes part of the compliance evidence set.

Forensic checklist (minimum):
- trace_id list for affected events
- provisioning-event.json blobs (raw and canonical)
- broker service logs (+5 minutes before/after each event)
- config diffs and commit SHA for broker and mapping rules
- SCIM/IdP endpoints and certificates used in the window
- KMS key usage logs for evidence buckets

Data residency and retention considerations:
- Attributes flagged as PII (email, phone) MUST be hashed with tenant-scoped salt before cross-region replication.
- Retention windows are mapped by environment and regulatory need:
  - dev/test: 1 year (hashed-only)
  - standard production: 7 years
  - regulated customers (contractual e.g., EU banking): customer-specific retention (may be 10+ years)
- Evidence replication: evidence buckets in primary region must be replicated to an audit-region when requested by compliance. Replication requests MUST include a justification ticket and be approved by InfoSec.

Secure SDLC guidance for broker changes:
- All mapping rule changes require an ADR-style change record with: description, risk assessment, automated test plan, and rollback steps.
- Unit tests must include negative tests for malformed assertions and property-based tests for attribute normalization.
- Integration tests (CI) must run a golden replay of provisioning events and assert no drift in canonical outputs.
- Feature flags: any change that alters role_claims mapping must be behind a canary and gated by a policy to automatically revert if anomalous increases in authorization failures are detected.

Compliance evidence packet template (what auditors expect):
1) Executive summary (who, what, when, impact)
2) Artifacts list (provisioning-event.json checksums + locations)
3) Key logs (trace_id + excerpts)
4) Configuration change history (git SHAs, PR links)
5) Approval timeline and tickets (change approvals, emergency approvals)
6) Post-incident review and remediation actions

Ownership and escalation:
- Broker service owner: identity-platform-team@redwood.com
- Evidence storage owner: security-compliance-evidence@redwood.com
- Incident commander (first 24h): oncall-iam (rotating)
- Escalation path: IAM oncall -> Security SRE -> Head of Security -> Legal (if cross-border PII involved)

Open considerations and roadmap items:
- Support for fine-grained entitlements mapped from external group graph (Q2 2025) with automated evidence snapshots for group changes.
- Improved PII redaction SDK for brokers so raw assertions never land in object storage unmasked.
- Automated compliance packaging: a one-click evidence export for auditors including signed checksums and KMS key proof.

Appendix: quick commands and snippets
- Download evidence blob by trace_id (CLI):
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-evidence/provisioning/2025/03/provisioning-event-{trace_id}.json ./ --profile redwood-audit

- Re-run canonicalization locally (developer harness):
  ./broker-harness --input ./fixtures/scim-events.json --output ./out/canonical.json --validate-only

- Example lifecycle policy (S3) for provisioning artifacts (JSON):
  {
    "Rules": [
      {"ID":"prod-retain-7y","Status":"Enabled","Prefix":"provisioning/","Expiration":{"Days":2555},"NoncurrentVersionExpiration":{"NoncurrentDays":2555}}
    ]
  }
